1. Purpose and system context
The synthetic powertrain control architecture coordinates driver demand, vehicle motion, engine state, torque
arbitration, and thermal protection. The document is designed to support entity extraction, relationship mapping, cited
question answering, and deterministic completeness checks.
1.1 Operational boundary
The logical boundary includes application software components only. Hardware drivers, operating-system internals,
calibration implementation, and production safety approval are outside the synthetic model.

5. Functional flows
5.1 Driver torque request flow
PedalPositionAdapter validates two synthetic pedal channels and publishes PedalPosition_pct through
If_PedalPosition. TorqueArbitrator consumes the value, considers EngineRunning from If_EngineState, and exposes
RequestedTorque_Nm through If_TorqueRequest. EngineControlCoordinator consumes the request and applies the
permitted torque.
5.2 Vehicle-speed flow
VehicleStateManager receives WheelSpeedRaw, calculates VehicleSpeed_kph, and publishes it every 20 ms through
PpVehicleSpeed. EngineControlCoordinator consumes the signal at RpVehicleSpeed for torque coordination.
5.3 Thermal limitation flow
ThermalProtectionManager publishes MaximumTorque_Nm and DeratingReason through If_ThermalLimit.
EngineControlCoordinator limits the requested torque whenever the thermal limit is lower than RequestedTorque_Nm.
